newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 38,550 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 43.862 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 31,250 tonnes, in the U.K. 3,000, in Denmark 3,000 and in Belgium 1,3000 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.636 million tonnes. This compares with the 43,750 tonnes awarded on March 13, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.647 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-August to be 43.862 Ecus per 100 kilos.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 30,000 and 60,000 tonnes versus 34,750 last week when the restitution was 43.835 Ecus.
